source_pages: printed p.440-441 / PDF 442-443, both pages read whole 2026-08-26
extraction_note: DEMAND-DRIVEN, 2026-08-26: the Avenida Primavera island needs finished ends, and the back-to-back depth groups are the only place in the book that prices them. Taken: the 2,2 cm ADJOINING END SIDE PANEL with 45-degree vertical edge, both pages. NOT taken from the same section: the L-shaped end side panel (printed p.436) and its three grip-recess variants (p.437-439), which need an L profile in 30_geometry that does not exist yet. NOT taken from the chapter: the Groove and lacquered-Intarsio edge pages (p.442-443), which price workmanship per square metre rather than pieces, and whose note - 'The Groove end side panel cannot be joined at 45 degrees with the door' - contradicts the geometry of everything in this file.
thickness_note: 2,2 cm, printed in the heading of every position. This is the FRONT thickness (Standards::FRONT_T_MM), and that is the whole point of the article: it lies in the plane of the doors it adjoins. The OTHER panel thickness in the book, 1,8 cm, is not an article at all - printed p.553 is titled 'Surcharge for finishing side panels, 1.8 cm thick | Replacing standard side panel'. It replaces the carcass's own side, so under rule 4 it draws nothing new and it has no code. Do not model the two as one object with a thickness field.
depth_note: EVERY GROUP PRINTS TWO NUMBERS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NUMBER. The label names the CARCASS depth the panel serves ('for 35-cm deep side panel + door thickness'); the 'd.' beside it is the depth the catalog DRAWS. Across all eight groups in this chapter the second is the first plus 2,2 per door face, rounded up - 35 -> 37,2 -> d.37,5; 70 -> 74,4 -> d.75; 124 -> 128,4 -> d.129. That arithmetic is DERIVED and is written here to explain the numbers, not to replace them: depth_mm below is the printed 'd.' verbatim. Whether 'd.' describes the finished end or the panel's own board is Elda Q21, and everything drawn at the end of a run depends on the answer.
label_collision_note: TWO GROUPS ON THIS PAGE CARRY THE SAME PRINTED LABEL. Both the d.102 and the d.107 group are printed 'for 62+35-cm deep side panel'. They cannot both be. The codes disagree with the label: at the heights where the letters are unambiguous the d.102 rows carry the prefixes this same chapter uses for a 62-deep panel and the d.107 rows carry the 67-deep prefixes, and the arithmetic in depth_note gives 62+35 -> 101,4 -> d.102 and 67+35 -> 106,4 -> d.107. The label is kept verbatim in printed_depth_label; the reading is Elda Q20. NOTE the letters are only a witness at the SHORT heights - from H.138 up, both groups use F-prefixes and are told apart by the trailing digits alone, which is rule 5 restated: a code is a lookup, never a decode.
surcharge_note: Charges printed beside the tables and NOT wired anywhere yet: vertical edge of door, each - 48 points up to H.72, 65 points from H.75 to H.140, 86 points above H.141; and 'Height reduction of side panel for side grip recess if an adjoined end side panel is present' - 84 points. Separately, printed p.549 prices an INCREASE of side panel depth, 62->67, 67->72 and 72->77, at 41 points a step. Points are commercial data and stay out of the object by Contract v2 1.2; they are recorded here because the exporter will need to find them.
finish_note: Finishes and price bands for every 2,2 cm end side panel are printed p.448-449, shared by all three collections. Bands 9 and 11 are '-' on every panel row in the chapter: those finish families are not made as panels. Not extracted - there is no appearance layer yet (M1.8).

end_panel_45.description: Adjoining end side panel, 2.2 cm thick - with 45 degree vertical edge
end_panel_45.handed_note: The ARTICLE has no hand. A panel does not open, so there is no hinge to hand, and the catalog prints one code for either end of a run. What IS handed is the 45-degree edge, which must face the door - and that follows from which end you place it at, so it is placement and not an attribute. The choice the catalog DOES price is a different one: which page you are on. See the two unit types in this file.

front_layout.note: A PANEL HAS NO FRONT. 'none' is stated rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs defaults a missing layout to 'single' and would hang a door leaf on a flat board. A default is not a source.

end_panel_45_opposite_hinge.choice_note: THIS IS A DIFFERENT ARTICLE, NOT A VARIANT. The two pages price the same heights and the same depth groups under different codes, and which one is right is decided by what the neighbouring unit does - drawers, a push-up door, or hinges away from the 45. That makes it the same kind of fact as hinge_side: never guessed, only chosen. The opposite-hinge page also carries FOUR back-to-back depth groups where the 45 page carries none, so an island end can only be ordered from this page.
